description: What an OVER clause REFERENCES is checked like anything else. Frostlake could not see inside one at all - a window call parses to a single expression node carrying its call TEXT, so the keys were invisible to the walk and a name resolving to nothing produced a perfectly ordinary result. The keys come from the PARSE TREE, which is the only place they survive. Each refusal lands at the key's OWN offset: a window ORDER BY key, a PARTITION BY key at one, two and three qualifier parts named in full, the call's ARGUMENT reported at the argument rather than at the call, and QUALIFY in both of its shapes - the windows written inline in it and its own predicate. All of it is COMPILE-time, so an EMPTY table is refused identically. A GROUPED query's window keys are walked too, in the select list and in QUALIFY alike, while the grouped shapes that must NOT be refused still read - which is why the walk runs against the BASE relation rather than the projected one: a GROUP BY key the select list never projects, and a raw aggregate over a column that is not a key at all. A call with SEVERAL arguments reports the argument that is wrong at its own offset HOWEVER IT IS SPACED, because the check re-forms the call to type its arguments and a fixed ', ' between them moved every later argument of a tightly written call. And every legitimate key still reads, a SELECT alias among them. Converted 1:1 from query/WindowKeyScopeTest (now retired); the Java flattened newlines out of the message before matching, so the converted steps pin the position and the identifier across a REAL newline.
